attributes.residual: NAMED MECHANISM, ONE INSTRUCTION, AND IT IS A RECORDED DEAD END. The prior label 'REGISTER_ONLY/SCHEDULE (allocator or scheduler residual)' was applied in bulk by the 2026-08-29 legacy import and is WRONG: regnorm reports 82 paired, 0 renaming, 1 STRUCTURAL, 0 unpaired, and the one row is an OPCODE difference, not a register one. At +0x00ac the target emits `mr r3,r28` and we emit `li r3,1`. Reading the target: `li r28,1` at +0x78 puts the constant 1 in r28, which is then used three times - `stw r28` to lbl_803445E0 at +0x80, `stw r28,0(r27)` at +0xa4, and the `mr r3,r28` at +0xac that supplies the else-branch value of `ok`. Our object ALREADY shares r28 for both stores; only the else-branch value is rematerialised. This is precisely the class capped in attempt.fn-8006e654-constant-copy-remat-park.20260831.v1: 'MWCC folds a copy from a variable whose value is a known constant into a fresh materialisation of that constant', a fold that record measured as surviving opt_propagation off, opt_common_subs off, chained assignment, combined for-init, STAGING LOCALS, storage-class hints, guard motion, nested-scope declaration init, inline identity ops and self-AND across three sessions. My probe was the staging-local form, i.e. one of the forms that record already killed - it should have been screened out before it was spent. WEBFRANK IS ALSO CLOSED here: the residual changes an OPCODE (mr vs li), so the register-recolor rule class cannot express it, and the count-asymmetric home-copy class is separately recorded as webfrank-ineligible (attempt.home-copy-coalescing-webfrank-ineligible.20260831.v1). CORRECT LABEL: STRUCTURAL, constant-copy rematerialisation, 1 instruction, source-unreachable by every form tried across four sessions.
